title: Types: consistent descriptions and realization
summary: Describe a tuple by a consistent collection of formulas, complete its description, and realize requests with parameters in elementary extensions.
abstract: No natural number is different from every natural-number numeral, although any finite list of those inequalities has a solution. Model theory treats such a collection of requests as a description that may be realized in a larger structure. A type records compatible first-order conditions on a tuple; a complete type decides every formula about it. We show that every compatible description can be completed and that a description using parameters from a structure is realized in an elementary extension exactly when each finite part can already be realized in the original structure. The proof explains why the original parameters must keep their full first-order meaning, and why a type need not have a solution in the model where it was first considered.
